action: Take RDM refrigeration controllers off the public internet and apply RDM's new firmware, as Pen Test Partners advises; see RDM advisory RDM-SA-2026-001.
exec: Exposed refrigeration controllers at retailers and food sites are a risk, so operators should check whether theirs are reachable from the internet.
plain: UK agencies and researchers worked to secure internet-exposed supermarket fridge controllers from RDM, after attacks on other makers' systems in Europe.

key_findings: Pen Test Partners says UK supermarkets mostly use RDM controllers and were largely not hit by the Danfoss incident.
Pen Test Partners says it is not publishing exploits or the discovery method.
RDM has released new firmware, per Pen Test Partners.
recommendations: Take controllers off the public internet.

summary: Pen Test Partners says a significant vulnerability in RDM refrigeration controllers, found by Neil McCourt of Omega Solutions and validated by its own researcher, led NCSC to issue an urgent alert to UK supermarkets. Security.NL, citing the BBC, reports a quiet operation by NCSC, FSA, Defra and others that took exposed RDM systems offline and patched them. No CVE or exploit details are published.
title: UK agencies and Pen Test Partners secure exposed RDM supermarket refrigeration controllers

validation.note: Pen Test Partners read in full; Security.NL read, relaying the BBC, which could not be loaded. Operation details rest on that relay.
